name: Recall Deck
shortDescription: Flashcards that flip in 3D, swipe to grade, and schedule themselves.
description: A flashcard deck with spaced repetition in one web page. Type the answer and the card tilts and turns in 3D to show the right one, with every letter you missed marked. Swipe right if you knew it or left to see it again, and the next card rises from the stack while a 30-day forecast re-tallies how many cards come back each day. Every card is scheduled with SM-2, the classic spaced repetition method. Browse searches and sorts the whole deck by tag and due date, and Forecast shows the month ahead, a half year of days studied, and how often you recall. Two themes: a cream index card with a red rule, and a slate blackboard in chalk. Progress stays in your browser, with export and import to carry it to another device. Your agent asks what you want to remember and writes the cards, then builds the page.
setup:
Ask the person, in one message: What do you want to remember? Paste the cards, or name the topic and you will write them. How many new cards a day, and do they want to type each answer?

Then copy inputs.example.json from the app folder to recall-deck.inputs.json in the project folder and edit it: deckName, the cards list (each with an id that never changes, a front, a back, tags, and an optional hint), newPerDay, typing (true or false), font (sans or serif), and theme (index-card, blackboard, or auto). progress is optional: delete it for a fresh deck, or put an exported progress file's state and log there. Delete the _notes object if you like; it only explains the keys.

Run python3 <app folder>/scripts/run.py from the project folder. It writes out/recall-deck/, which any static file server can host. No keys are needed, and nothing leaves the person's browser.
